Questions: Creta vs Venue — which one should I choose?
Answers: Hyundai Venue: A compact S U V with city-friendly dimensions, convenient parking and connected technology. It suits first-time S U V buyers, everyday city commuters and customers looking for a more accessible entry point into Hyundai's S U V range. Hyundai Creta: A larger S U V with more cabin space and a broader range of comfort and technology features. It offers multiple powertrain choices, including petrol, diesel and electric options across the Creta range. Recommendation: Choose the Venue for compact city practicality and budget-conscious ownership. Consider the Creta if you want more space, features and greater family versatility.

Questions: Creta vs Alcazar — what's the difference?
Answers: Hyundai Creta: A 5 seater mid-size S U V that offers a spacious cabin, modern technology and a wide range of comfort and convenience features. Hyundai Alcazar: A three-row S U V available in 6 seater and 7 seater configurations, offering additional passenger space and a captain-seat option in the 6 seater layout. Recommendation: Choose the Creta if five seats meet your needs. Choose the Alcazar if you need three-row seating and greater flexibility for a larger family.

Questions: Exter vs Venue — which is better?
Answers: Hyundai Exter: A compact entry-level S U V designed for easy city driving and convenient parking. It offers modern features and is available with petrol and C N G powertrain options. Hyundai Venue: A larger compact S U V that offers more cabin space along with multiple powertrain choices, including turbo-petrol and diesel options. Recommendation: Choose the Exter if you prioritise budget, city driving and easy parking. Consider the Venue if you want a larger S U V with more space and broader engine options.

Questions: i20 vs Grand i10 Nios — what's the difference?
Answers: Hyundai Grand i 10 Nios: A compact hatchback designed for practical and efficient city driving, with petrol and C N G options. It suits buyers looking for an everyday commuter. Hyundai i 20: A premium hatchback with a more spacious cabin and a wider range of comfort, connectivity and technology features. Buyers looking for a sportier driving experience can also consider the i 20 N Line. Recommendation: Choose the Grand i 10 Nios for value-focused city commuting. Consider the i 20 if you want a more premium and feature-rich hatchback.

Questions: Verna vs Creta — sedan or SUV?
Answers: Hyundai Verna: A premium mid-size sedan with sporty styling, a comfortable cabin, advanced technology and available A D A S features. Its turbo-petrol option adds stronger performance, making it well suited to buyers who enjoy sedan comfort and frequent highway driving. Hyundai Creta: A mid-size S U V with an elevated seating position, spacious cabin and strong S U V presence. It suits buyers looking for everyday practicality, family space and versatility across city and highway journeys. Recommendation: Choose the Verna if you prefer sedan comfort, sporty performance and highway cruising. Consider the Creta if you want an elevated driving position, S U V styling and greater everyday versatility.

Questions: Creta Electric vs Creta petrol — which should I pick?
Answers: Hyundai Creta Electric: A good choice if you want an all-electric driving experience, lower per-kilometre energy costs and have convenient access to home, workplace or public charging. Hyundai Creta Petrol: A practical choice if you prefer quick refuelling, regularly take longer or less predictable journeys, or do not have convenient charging access. Recommendation: Choose the Creta Electric for regular city use with reliable charging access. Choose the Creta Petrol if you prioritise refuelling convenience and flexibility for varied travel.
